in_hebrew.name: יוהנה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא חנון, ה' הוא חנון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יוהנה הוא נגזר מהשם העברי 'יוֹחָנָן', שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא חנון' או 'ה' הוא חנון'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'יוֹ' שפירושו 'אלוהים' ו'חָנָן' שפירושו 'חנון'. השם יוהנה הוא מקור השם היווני 'Ἰωάννης' (יואניס) והלטיני 'Ioannes', ששימשו כבסיס לשמות רבים בשפות אירופיות.

in_greek.name: Ιωάννα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιωάννα προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα 'יוֹחָנָן' (Yōḥānān), που σημαίνει 'Θεός ελεήμων' ή 'ο Κύριος ελεήμων'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'יוֹ' (Yō), που σημαίνει 'Θεός', και 'חָנָן' (ḥānān), που σημαίνει 'ελεήμων'. Το όνομα Ιωάννα ήταν γνωστό στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και χρησιμοποιήθηκε από πολλές αγίες και μάρτυρες.

in_latin.name: Iohanna
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Iohanna derivatur a nomine hebraico 'יוֹחָנָן' (Yōḥānān), quod significat 'Deus misericors' vel 'Dominus misericors'. Nomen constat ex duabus vocibus: 'יוֹ' (Yō), quod significat 'Deus', et 'חָנָן' (ḥānān), quod significat 'misericors'. Nomen Iohanna usitatum erat in Ecclesia primitiva et multis sanctis et martyribus datum est.

in_english.name: Yohanna
in_english.meaning: God is gracious, God is merciful
in_english.long_meaning: The name Yohanna originates from the Hebrew name 'יוֹחָנָן' (Yōḥānān), meaning 'God is gracious' or 'God is merciful'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'יוֹ' (Yō), meaning 'God', and 'חָנָן' (ḥānān), meaning 'gracious' or 'merciful'. The name Yohanna was adopted into Greek as 'Ἰωάννης' (Iōannēs) and into Latin as 'Ioannes', and has been used in various forms across Christian cultures. It is associated with several biblical figures, including John the Baptist and John the Apostle, and has been borne by numerous saints and martyrs throughout history.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Yohanna" holds a rich cultural history, stemming from the Hebrew tradition. It was notably used in the New Testament for John the Baptist and John the Beloved Disciple, adding a biblical significance to the name. In Christian communities across the world, children given the name Yohanna are often associated with grace, sacrifice, and spiritual wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Yohanna is deeply rooted in spiritual meaning as it translates to 'God is gracious'. For Christians, it serves as a constant reminder of God's boundless grace and generosity. Students of the faith with this name may feel an added responsibility to embody the divine qualities of love, compassion, and humility, honoring not only their own identity but also the deity attributed to their name.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yohanna, a Hebrew name meaning "God is gracious," is often given to girls in the Christian faith. This name conveys a sense of divine favor and blessings, emphasizing the belief that God's grace is abundant and continuously bestowed upon His children.
